hints: Notice the same energy is expressed per unit mass in $\text{MJ kg}^{-1}$ and per unit volume in $\text{GJ m}^{-3}$.
Recall density $\rho = m/V$ links mass and volume, so dividing energy per volume by energy per mass leaves $\text{kg m}^{-3}$.
Convert $34.9 \text{ GJ m}^{-3}$ to $34900 \text{ MJ m}^{-3}$ before dividing by $41.8 \text{ MJ kg}^{-1}$.
walkthrough: Write the two given values with SI prefixes: $41.8 \text{ MJ kg}^{-1} = 41.8 \times 10^6 \text{ J kg}^{-1}$ and $34.9 \text{ GJ m}^{-3} = 34.9 \times 10^9 \text{ J m}^{-3}$.
Use $\rho = m/V$. Energy per unit volume divided by energy per unit mass gives $(E/V)/(E/m) = m/V = \rho$.
Set up $\rho = (34.9 \times 10^9 \text{ J m}^{-3}) / (41.8 \times 10^6 \text{ J kg}^{-1})$.
Simplify to $\rho = (34.9/41.8) \times 10^3 \text{ kg m}^{-3} \approx 0.835 \times 10^3 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$.
Rewrite in standard form as $8.35 \times 10^2 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$. This is option A.

options.A: Dividing $34.9 \times 10^9 \text{ J m}^{-3}$ by $41.8 \times 10^6 \text{ J kg}^{-1}$ gives about $835 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$.
options.B: This is the inverse ratio $41.8/34.9$ with prefixes mishandled, giving mass per energy inverted instead of density.
options.C: This results from dividing without converting $\text{GJ}$ to $\text{MJ}$, so it is too large by a factor of $1000$.
options.D: This results from taking the inverse ratio and omitting the $\text{GJ}$ to $\text{MJ}$ conversion, so it is far too large.
